questionText:
Consider a dynamic hashing approach for 4-bit integer keys:
1. There is a main hash table of size 4.
2. The 2 least significant bits of a key is used to index into the main hash table.
3. Initially, the main hash table entries are empty.
4. Thereafter, when more keys are hashed into it, to resolve collisions, the set of all keys corresponding to a main hash table entry is organized as a binary tree that grows on demand.
5. First, the $3^{\text{rd}}$ least significant bit is used to divide the keys into left and right subtrees.
6. To resolve more collisions, each node of the binary tree is further sub-divided into left and right subtrees based on the $4^{\text{th}}$ least significant bit.
7. A split is done only if it is needed, i.e., only when there is a collision.

Consider the following state of the hash table.

Which of the following sequences of key insertions can cause the above state of the hash table (assume the keys are in decimal notation)?
explanation:
To determine the correct sequence of insertions, let us convert the decimal keys to 4-bit binary representation ($b_4 b_3 b_2 b_1$):
• $1 = 0001_2$
• $4 = 0100_2$
• $5 = 0101_2$
• $6 = 0110_2$
• $7 = 0111_2$
• $9 = 1001_2$
• $10 = 1010_2$
• $13 = 1101_2$
• $14 = 1110_2$

Analyzing Hash Table Indexing Rules:
1. Index in main hash table is determined by the 2 LSBs ($b_2 b_1$).
2. Split at $3^{\text{rd}}$ LSB ($b_3$): 0 goes Left, 1 goes Right.
3. Split at $4^{\text{th}}$ LSB ($b_4$): 0 goes Left, 1 goes Right.

Target Hash Table State:
• Index 00: Empty.
• Index 01: Left subtree ($b_3=0$) contains 1 leaf (key 9). Right subtree ($b_3=1$) is split into $b_4=0$ (key 5) and $b_4=1$ (key 13).
• Index 10: Split at $b_3$ into $b_3=0$ (key 10) and $b_3=1$ (key 6).
• Index 11: Contains 1 leaf (key 7).

Trace for Option C (10, 9, 6, 7, 5, 13):
1. Insert 10 ($1010_2$): 2 LSBs = 10 $\implies$ Placed at Index 10.
2. Insert 9 ($1001_2$): 2 LSBs = 01 $\implies$ Placed at Index 01.
3. Insert 6 ($0110_2$): 2 LSBs = 10 $\implies$ Collides with 10. Split on $b_3$: 10 ($b_3=0$) goes left, 6 ($b_3=1$) goes right.
4. Insert 7 ($0111_2$): 2 LSBs = 11 $\implies$ Placed at Index 11.
5. Insert 5 ($0101_2$): 2 LSBs = 01 $\implies$ Collides with 9. Split on $b_3$: 9 ($b_3=0$) goes left, 5 ($b_3=1$) goes right.
6. Insert 13 ($1101_2$): 2 LSBs = 01, $b_3=1 \implies$ Collides with 5. Split on $b_4$: 5 ($b_4=0$) goes left, 13 ($b_4=1$) goes right.

This sequence exactly reproduces the given hash table state. Hence, Option C is correct.
